quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line on your side, when may you pass?

options.text: If you are on an expressway.

questions.correctAnswerText: If traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Running the car in the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops waste fuel because you use extra gas to speed back up. Looking ahead lets you slow down slowly or change lanes to avoid hard braking, which saves gas.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit.
Drive close behind the car ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When rain makes it hard to see, slow down. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If rain is very heavy, pull over and stop until it clears up.

questions.question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow line to pass another car?

options.text: Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the car ahead is going below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Two solid yellow lines mean no traffic may cross them, except to turn into a driveway or business entrance. You cannot pass over solid yellow lines.

questions.question: When may you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You may cross them to pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What is your blind spot?

options.text: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
The area directly behind your vehicle.
The area you see in your rearview mirror.
The area you see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: When may you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when you see warning signals. These include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a person signaling, or a train's whistle. Never go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road or driveway?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other cars.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out quickly to blend in with traffic.
Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic already on the roadway.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles, in bad weather, in heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind motorcycles or bicycles, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: If you get stuck in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out and walk to find help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car so rescuers can find you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car so rescuers can find you.
questions.explanation: If you are stuck in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay with your vehicle. Walking in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A sharp right turn is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sharp right turn is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a sharp right turn is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use your brakes right away.
Slow down gradually and pull to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: During a tire blowout, take your foot off the gas. Do not brake right away. Slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: What does this sign shape and color indicate?
questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs are only used to mark no passing zones.

questions.question: You are driving uphill toward a heavy truck. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be driving slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to pass the truck safely.
You may not be able to pass the truck legally.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often drive slower than the speed limit, especially uphill. Passing may be unsafe due to limited visibility. On hills, passing is also illegal in many cases. Use caution when approaching large vehicles from behind.

questions.question: Another car is about to hit you. What should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. Sound your horn if you think another driver is about to hit you.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: The same as a stop sign.
You do not have to stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: You see a sign saying "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should go 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: When you see a "Reduced speed" sign with a new speed limit, that speed limit begins right at the sign.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before you turn or change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Never depend on mirrors alone.

questions.question: How should you prepare for hazards ahead on the road?

options.text: Constantly look at the entire road and both sides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Constantly look at the entire road and both sides.
questions.explanation: Good driving depends on spotting problems before you reach them. Look far ahead and scan the entire road, including the sides. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The start of a reduced speed zone.
The reduced speed zone is over.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone is over.
questions.explanation: Do not drive faster than the school zone speed limit during the posted times. An "End school zone" sign marks the end of the reduced speed zone.

questions.question: You must yield to emergency vehicles:

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: Drivers should pay extra attention to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers didn't see motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians even when looking. These are smaller, move faster, and have less noticeable lights. Stay alert to spot them on the road.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Traffic is merging from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is entering from the right.

questions.question: Orange signs mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond signs warn of work zones on the highway. They have black letters or symbols and tell you that workers are near the road.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same as:
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: At a flashing red light, you must stop and let other traffic go first.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the right lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes then back up to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make sudden last-minute turns. Drive to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a highway and want to move left. You should:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in your blind spot. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your hazard lights or horn when needed.

questions.question: You may carefully drive through a yellow light if:

options.text: An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
You already entered the intersection when the light turned yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You already entered the intersection when the light turned yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians.
questions.explanation: At night, pedestrians are harder to see than signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid crashes when driving on ice or snow?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle to improve grip.
Leave highways as quickly as possible.
Drive slower and leave more space between cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower and leave more space between cars.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snow or ice. Reducing speed and increasing distance between cars are the best ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.

questions.question: When turning left, you have the right-of-way at which traffic signal?
questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of the following except:

options.text: How much time passes between drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, time between drinks, and your weight. It does not depend on the type of drink, your fitness level, or how well you can handle alcohol.

questions.question: What is the safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down entering the curve, speed up leaving the curve.
Keep the same speed throughout the curve.
Speed up entering the curve, slow down leaving the curve.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down entering the curve, speed up leaving the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before the curve and gradually speed up as you exit. Speeding up as you enter makes it harder to control your car.

questions.question: After a school bus stops to let children off:

options.text: Wait until children wave at you before moving.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After a school bus stops with lights flashing, watch for children on the side of the road. Always drive carefully near children.
